sections.overview: The giant phantom jelly is a large scyphozoan of the deep open ocean.
sections.identification: Its bell can exceed one metre across, with four ribbon-like oral arms reaching about ten metres.
sections.habitat: It has been observed from near the surface to about 6700 metres, across oceans except the Arctic.
sections.diet: Its likely prey include plankton and small fishes, which its broad oral arms can hold.
sections.behavior: It is rarely seen; a 2019 dataset compiled just over a century of sparse observations.
sections.reproduction: The consulted field accounts do not describe its reproductive cycle.
sections.ecology: A fish has been filmed sheltering among its oral arms, an unusual deep-sea association.
sections.conservation: The sources describe its rarity of observation but provide no global threat assessment.
